{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the Mediterranean|Mediterranean]] | [[Cookbook:Middle Eastern cuisines|Middle Eastern cuisines]]

== Ingredients ==

*½ cup [[Cookbook:Bulgur|bulghur]] wheat (fine grind is best, medium grind acceptable)
*2 bunches [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]] (flat leaf or curly Italian)
*1 bunch [[Cookbook:Green Onion|green onion]]
*At least 2 cups [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
*5–6 stalks fresh [[Cookbook:Mint|mint]]
*2–3 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemons]], or to taste
*[[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]]
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
*[[Cookbook:Cucumber|Cucumbers]] (optional)
*Romaine [[Cookbook:Lettuce|lettuce]] leaves (garnish and scoopers, optional)
*Fresh [[Cookbook:Grape Leaf|grape leaves]] (optional)

== Procedure ==

#Soak the bulghur wheat in at least three times its volume of cold water. Fine grind only needs a half hour of soaking. Medium grind needs longer. Bulghur wheat has already been parboiled before cracking or grinding, so it doesn’t need further cooking to be edible in tabbouli.
#Drain bulghur. 
#[[Cookbook:Chopping|Chop]] the parsley leaves, green onions, mint, tomatoes and cucumbers.
#Chop the parsley quite fine, using a knife, not food processor. 
#Mix veggies and bulghur together. Douse with strained lemon juice. If you are not ready to serve immediately, then cover and hold in a cool place. Do NOT add salt and olive oil until immediately before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* You may garnish with more diced tomatoes and/or diced cucumber, and insert lettuce or fresh grape leaves around the sides of the bowl. Use green leaves to scoop up the salad, popping leaf and salad into mouth.
